title: Non-invasive transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) to reduce perioperative stress responses and improve early recovery after radical prostatectomy – a prospective, randomized, sham-controlled three-arm pilot study
summary:
Surgery to remove the prostate because of prostate cancer is a major physical and emotional burden for many men. Worries about the cancer, the operation and possible consequences such as urine leakage or changes in sexual function can cause considerable stress. This stress can be measured through a natural stress hormone in saliva and may affect pain, sleep and recovery after surgery.

One possible support is a gentle electrical stimulation at the ear. A small electrode on the outer ear stimulates a nerve that helps the body calm down. The method is approved, not painful and well tolerated. Whether it helps patients around prostate surgery has not been studied so far.

In this preliminary study, we first want to find out whether the treatment can be carried out well in everyday hospital routine and how patients accept it. We also want to estimate how much the stress hormone, anxiety, pain and recovery change. These results will help to plan a larger study properly.

Participants are assigned by chance to one of three groups. The first group receives the real stimulation, the second a dummy stimulation with the same device, and the third the usual care without a device. In the two device groups, participants do not know which stimulation they receive. Stimulation is given six times for 30 minutes each, from the day before surgery to the second day after. In all groups, saliva samples are taken and short questionnaires are completed at fixed times. Usual medical care remains unchanged in all groups.

interventions.name: Active transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS): In addition to standard perioperative care, patients receive 6 stimulation sessions of 30 minutes each using a CE-marked device (Nurosym®) via an ear electrode placed at the tragus (25 Hz, pulse width 200–250 µs, intensity individually

Sham stimulation: In addition to standard perioperative care, procedures identical to arm 1 (application of the same device, same schedule of 6 sessions of 30 minutes each), but with subtherapeutic, non-effective stimulation intensity. Patients are blinded to allocation (active vs. sham).

Control: Standard perioperative care without device application. Saliva samples and questionnaires are collected at the same time points as in arms 1 and 2. Open-label arm; blinding is not possible in this arm.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Histologically confirmed localized prostate cancer (cT1–cT3a, N0, M0)
- Scheduled elective radical prostatectomy (robot-assisted or open)
- Written informed consent after detailed information
- Sufficient language comprehension for questionnaires and informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Known disease or prior damage of the vagus nerve
- Active implants (e.g. cardiac pacemaker, cochlear implant)
- Severe psychiatric disorder (e.g. active psychosis, severe depression)
- Systemic glucocorticoid therapy within the last 4 weeks
- Skin lesions in the area of the cymba conchae
- Participation in another interventional study
- History of epilepsy
